verbatim_locators.source_fulltext_indexed_evidence: Structured Europe PMC XML, the supplementary PDF with its text layer, and all five figure images are local and fingerprinted; Figures 2 and 4 were inspected as images and Figures 1, 3 and 5 were opened and viewed.
verbatim_locators.abstract_anchoring_waived: No textual locator is anchored to the abstract; the abstract's enzyme-capacity figures are compared with the Results text and Figure 4 in the entries above.
verbatim_locators.note: 2026-11-01 reconciliation reading (QUESTION_DRIVEN: the reader held the IT15 P4 package verdict). Each proposition is labelled as an external methodological precedent statement, not WWOX evidence.

entries.proposition: EXTERNAL METHODOLOGICAL PRECEDENT, NOT WWOX EVIDENCE (SH-SY5Y, pharmacological respiratory inhibitors): The tracer was supplied after the inhibitor was removed, so the labelling reports a post-exposure state and not flux during inhibition.
entries.snippet: were not re-added to the serum-free, glucose-free DMEM
entries.anchor: Methods 4.2, last sentences before the dosing paragraph

entries.proposition: EXTERNAL METHODOLOGICAL PRECEDENT, NOT WWOX EVIDENCE (SH-SY5Y, pharmacological respiratory inhibitors): All five exposures are compared with one shared vehicle-control triplicate; no separate ethanol-vehicle arm was run.
entries.snippet: all five exposure conditions are compared against that one control triplicate; separate vehicle-matched controls for the saline- and ethanol-dissolved compounds were not run

entries.proposition: EXTERNAL METHODOLOGICAL PRECEDENT, NOT WWOX EVIDENCE (SH-SY5Y, pharmacological respiratory inhibitors): The route assignment of glutamate positions is first-turn only: PDH labels glutamate C4/C5 and PC labels C2/C3.
entries.snippet: carbon entering through pyruvate dehydrogenase labels glutamate C4 and C5, whereas carbon entering through pyruvate carboxylase labels glutamate C2 and C3

entries.proposition: EXTERNAL METHODOLOGICAL PRECEDENT, NOT WWOX EVIDENCE (SH-SY5Y, pharmacological respiratory inhibitors): At the 24 h endpoint scrambling is assumed substantially complete and no correction was applied, so C4/C3 is an integrated indicator and not a route-specific measurement.
entries.snippet: At the 24 h labelling endpoint used here, the system has passed well beyond that point, so scrambling must be assumed to be substantially complete.

entries.proposition: EXTERNAL METHODOLOGICAL PRECEDENT, NOT WWOX EVIDENCE (SH-SY5Y, pharmacological respiratory inhibitors): Oligomycin: glutamate C3 (PC-associated) rose to 197.7 percent of control while glutamate C4 (PDH-associated) stayed at 107.2 percent; n = 3 and the shared-control Dunnett contrast is the quoted p.
entries.snippet: The PC-associated glutamate C3 readout rose to 197.7 +/− 8.1% of control

entries.proposition: EXTERNAL METHODOLOGICAL PRECEDENT, NOT WWOX EVIDENCE (SH-SY5Y, pharmacological respiratory inhibitors): The authors state that the PC and PDH assays report capacity under saturating cofactors, not in-cell flux (PDH assay, extract-level, relative to control).
entries.snippet: so the readout reports the decarboxylating capacity of the extract rather than in-cell flux

entries.proposition: EXTERNAL METHODOLOGICAL PRECEDENT, NOT WWOX EVIDENCE (SH-SY5Y, pharmacological respiratory inhibitors): PC and PDH assays were run on protein-preserving extracts prepared in parallel, not on the perchloric-acid metabolite extracts.
entries.snippet: the PC and PDH assays were therefore performed on protein-preserving extracts prepared in parallel from the same biological replicates

entries.proposition: EXTERNAL METHODOLOGICAL PRECEDENT, NOT WWOX EVIDENCE (SH-SY5Y, pharmacological respiratory inhibitors): Text value of the enzyme-capacity result under oligomycin (approximately 138 percent PC and 60 percent PDH); see the Figure 4C,D entry for what the bars show.
entries.snippet: Under oligomycin, PC activity rose to approximately 138% of control (p < 0.01), while PDH activity fell to approximately 60% (Figure 4C,D).

entries.proposition: EXTERNAL METHODOLOGICAL PRECEDENT, NOT WWOX EVIDENCE (SH-SY5Y, pharmacological respiratory inhibitors): The medium data are descriptive: normalisation and multiplicity handling are stated by the authors as not fully specified.
entries.snippet: the normalisation and the multiplicity treatment of the medium data are not fully specified

entries.proposition: EXTERNAL METHODOLOGICAL PRECEDENT, NOT WWOX EVIDENCE (SH-SY5Y, pharmacological respiratory inhibitors): The authors state that respiratory inhibition is inferred, not demonstrated: no OCR, ATP, membrane potential, NAD+/NADH, ROS or complex activity was measured.
entries.snippet: so respiratory inhibition is inferred from the pharmacology of the compounds

entries.proposition: EXTERNAL METHODOLOGICAL PRECEDENT, NOT WWOX EVIDENCE (SH-SY5Y, pharmacological respiratory inhibitors): Sensitivity: at n = 3 per group the design detects only large standardised effects, so non-significant comparisons are uninformative, not evidence of no effect.
entries.snippet: this design detects standardised effects of approximately d = 3.1 or larger

entries.proposition: EXTERNAL METHODOLOGICAL PRECEDENT, NOT WWOX EVIDENCE (SH-SY5Y, pharmacological respiratory inhibitors): MPTP is the weakest condition: partial Complex I lesion in undifferentiated SH-SY5Y (low MAO-B) and most comparisons do not survive the shared-control analysis.
entries.snippet: MPTP is the weakest of the five exposures under this analysis

entries.proposition: EXTERNAL METHODOLOGICAL PRECEDENT, NOT WWOX EVIDENCE (SH-SY5Y, pharmacological respiratory inhibitors): The authors place a design boundary on the result: undifferentiated SH-SY5Y is not a disease model, none of the compounds is a therapeutic agent.
entries.snippet: None of the five compounds is a therapeutic agent, and nothing in these data speaks to therapeutic benefit or risk in patients.

entries.proposition: EXTERNAL METHODOLOGICAL PRECEDENT, NOT WWOX EVIDENCE (SH-SY5Y, pharmacological respiratory inhibitors): Data availability: raw free induction decays only on request; no repository deposit is named.
entries.snippet: Raw NMR free induction decays are available from the corresponding author on reasonable request.

entries.proposition: EXTERNAL METHODOLOGICAL PRECEDENT, NOT WWOX EVIDENCE (SH-SY5Y, pharmacological respiratory inhibitors): Succinate was not detected in control extracts, so no ratio or test exists for that row; labelled succinate under 3-NP is qualitative.
entries.snippet: succinate was not detected in control extracts, so no ratio to control and no significance test can be computed for that row

entries.proposition: EXTERNAL METHODOLOGICAL PRECEDENT, NOT WWOX EVIDENCE (SH-SY5Y, pharmacological respiratory inhibitors): Supplementary Table S1 states the design's minimum detectable effect (d = 3.07 at n = 3 per group, alpha 0.05, 80 percent power).
entries.snippet: minimum detectable effect for this design is d = 3.07
entries.anchor: Supplementary Table S1 header note, page 1 of the supplementary PDF

entries.proposition: EXTERNAL METHODOLOGICAL PRECEDENT, NOT WWOX EVIDENCE (SH-SY5Y, pharmacological respiratory inhibitors): Supplementary Table S2 documents a reassignment of the 34.6 ppm resonance from a GABA annotation to succinate C2/C3 in the primary integral file.
entries.snippet: The primary integral tables (13C_quantitation_.xls) annotate two resonances under a numbering convention that counts from the amine-bearing
entries.anchor: Supplementary Table S2, row ~34.6 ppm, page 3 of the supplementary PDF

entries.proposition: EXTERNAL METHODOLOGICAL PRECEDENT, NOT WWOX EVIDENCE (SH-SY5Y, pharmacological respiratory inhibitors): Figure 4C,D as drawn: PDH capacity bars are significantly below control only for azide (about 65 percent, one asterisk) and oligomycin (about 65 percent, two asterisks); PC capacity bars are above control in all five exposures (MPTP about 147 and 3-NP about 131 with two asterisks, antimycin A about 120 and azide about 111 with one asterisk, oligomycin about 133 with two asterisks). So the PC-capacity rise is not specific to oligomycin, and the bar values (read off the axis, approximate) are lower than the text figures of about 138 percent PC and 60 percent PDH.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 4C (change in PDH activity) and 4D (change in PC activity), bars with asterisks as printed: PDH azide about 65 one asterisk, oligomycin about 65 two asterisks, other groups not marked; PC MPTP about 147 two asterisks, 3-NP about 131 two, antimycin A about 120 one, azide about 111 one, oligomycin about 133 two. Values read from the axis, approximate.

entries.proposition: EXTERNAL METHODOLOGICAL PRECEDENT, NOT WWOX EVIDENCE (SH-SY5Y, pharmacological respiratory inhibitors): Figure 2A as drawn: the heatmap prints succinate as det. 28.0x under 3-NP, det. 1.0x under antimycin A, det. 0.9x under oligomycin and n.d. under MPTP and azide; the control is not detected, so these are not ratios to control. Figure 2B: control and MPTP replicates sit on the right of PC1, azide and antimycin A on the left, oligomycin lower on PC2.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 2A succinate row cell labels: MPTP n.d., 3-NP det. 28.0x, AntiA det. 1.0x, Azide n.d., Oligo det. 0.9x; Figure 2B PCA, three replicate points per group, PERMANOVA pseudo-F = 18.77 p = 0.0001 printed on the panel.
